question: Two banks, A and B, offered loans at 3.5% and 7.5% per annum, respectively. Ashish borrowed an amount of ₹2,60,000 from each bank. Find the positive difference (in ₹) between the amounts of simple interest paid to the two banks by Ashish after 3 years.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Directly calculate the difference in Simple Interest using the difference in their interest rates.

Difference in interest rates = 7.5% − 3.5% = 4%

Difference in Simple Interest = (Principal × Difference in Rate × Time) ÷ 100

Difference in SI = (2,60,000 × 4 × 3) ÷ 100

Difference in SI = 2,600 × 12 = 31,200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹31,200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹2,60,000

Rate for Bank A (RA) = 3.5% per annum

Rate for Bank B (RB) = 7.5% per annum

Time (T) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 

 

 

 

 
 
 
 P = ₹2,60,000
 T = 3 Years
 
 
 
 Bank A: 3.5%
 SI = ₹27,300
 
 
 
 Bank B: 7.5%
 SI = ₹58,500
 
 
 
 Difference
 ₹31,200

**Calculations:**

⇒ Simple Interest paid to Bank A = (2,60,000 × 3.5 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ SI for Bank A = 2,600 × 10.5 = ₹27,300

⇒ Simple Interest paid to Bank B = (2,60,000 × 7.5 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ SI for Bank B = 2,600 × 22.5 = ₹58,500

⇒ Difference in Simple Interest = SI for Bank B − SI for Bank A

⇒ Difference in Simple Interest = ₹58,500 − ₹27,300 = ₹31,200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹31,200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Difference Formula for SI

When the principal and time period are constant, the difference in simple interest depends entirely on the difference in the given interest rates: ΔSI = P × ΔR × T ÷ 100.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the interest is calculated only on the initial principal. In Compound Interest, interest is calculated on both the principal and the accumulated interest of previous periods.

Compound Interest Formula

The amount after T years at compound interest is given by A = P(1 + R÷100)T, and the final compound interest is CI = A − P.
